QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_17

question.text: A 3-year bond with 10% annual coupon, face value Rs. 100, required yield 9%, has semi-annual compounding. What is the approximate convexity?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook gives the same 3-year, 10% coupon, semi-annual compounding, 9% yield example and computes convexity as 8.2135, which rounds to 8.21. The Trap: Convexity values for semi-annual bonds must be divided by 4 (=2²) to make them comparable with annual bonds. Using the raw sum without this adjustment gives an inflated figure. Note: Positive convexity makes the price gain for a yield fall greater than the price loss for an equal yield rise.
